claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation through multistage thermo-mechanical processing can simultaneously produce ultrahigh yield strength and tensile ductility in a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy.
The investigated alloy has composition (W1.5Ni2.25Fe)95Ta5 (at.%) and is based on a supersaturated solid-solution matrix.
The initial alloy exhibits poor room-temperature ductility because of brittle phases or an absence of coherent strengthening mechanisms.
Controlling the Ni/Fe ratio between 2 and 4 suppresses formation of the topologically close-packed μ phase at phase boundaries.
Adding 5 at.% Ta creates a supersaturated solid-solution matrix suitable for coherent precipitation.

Multistage thermo-mechanical processing sequentially and independently precipitates coherent Ni3Ta-based δ with D0a structure and γ″ with D022 structure over different phase-transition temperature ranges.
Controlled cooling rates and aging steps are required to achieve independent precipitation of δ and γ″.
The processed structure contains two distinct coherent precipitate populations, δ and γ″.
The δ and γ″ precipitates are dispersed in a BCC matrix.
Coherent precipitate-matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that otherwise promote premature crack initiation.
The hierarchical precipitation structure induces multistage strain hardening and delays localized plastic instability.
Precipitation hardening maintains high strength while coherent-interface-mediated deformation enhances ductility.
The SCCP alloy achieves approximately 2.15 GPa yield strength and approximately 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The SCCP alloy retains approximately 1.05 GPa yield strength at 800°C.
RHEAs with an ordered B2+BCC microstructure commonly have high yield strength but poor room-temperature ductility because a continuous ordered B2 matrix is brittle.
Conventional single-phase BCC RHEAs generally have less than 5% room-temperature ductility because they lack coherent strengthening mechanisms.
The SCCP strategy is applicable to tungsten-based refractory HEAs with controlled Ni/Fe ratios and Ta additions but may fail if μ or other topologically close-packed phases form.
The exact precipitation windows may vary with minor compositional fluctuations.
The long-term thermal stability of the coherent precipitates above 800°C has not been validated.
Coherent δ and γ″ precipitates should occur only in the SCCP-processed sample and not in the single-step-aged control.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that SCCP processing will exceed 2 GPa strength while retaining high ductility, but the experiment says that failure of the SCCP sample to exceed 2 GPa and 10% ductility would support the hypothesis. That result would instead contradict the predicted outcome.

The structure is called dual-phase while simultaneously identifying a BCC matrix plus two distinct precipitate phases, δ and γ″, which describes at least three phases. The evidence supports dual coherent precipitate populations, not necessarily a dual-phase microstructure.
